draft.title: Community health resources
card: Community health resources are services in an area that support people's health. Examples are GPs, community health centres, helplines and school counsellors.
a doctor who treats common health problems, gives check-ups and refers patients to specialists.
a phone or online service where people can talk to a trained person, often at any hour and without giving their name.
A resource only helps people who can reach it. Cost, distance, transport, language, opening hours and not knowing the service exists can all stop people from using it.
draft.remember: A health service only helps people who can reach and use it.

a.q: Which of these is a community health resource?
opts: A community health centre that offers local check-ups
A school rule that bans phones in class
A national law that sets the speed limit on roads
A gym membership paid for by a student
a.why: A community health centre is a local service that supports people's health. The other options are a rule, a law and a private purchase, and none of them is a service in an area that people can go to for health support.
a.clue: Look for a service that people in an area can go to for help.

b.q: Priya lives on a farm far from town in country NSW. The nearest GP is a two-hour drive away. Which is the main reason she may find it hard to use this resource?
opts: Distance and travel make the service hard to reach
The GP service is not a community health resource
GPs only treat people who live in large cities
Helplines cannot be used by people in country areas
b.why: The GP is a community health resource, but the two-hour drive makes it hard for Priya to reach. The tempting wrong option says GPs only treat city people, which is false: the problem is access, not who the GP is allowed to treat.
b.clue: The service exists, so think about what stands between Priya and it.

a.best: A community health centre that offers local check-ups

b.best: Distance and travel make the service hard to reach

problems.detail: The distractor 'A national law that sets the speed limit on roads' implies something false. In Australia, speed limits are set by state and territory road rules, not by a national law.
Too easy for Year 11. The stem states the distance outright, and the other three options are plainly false or absurd, so a student can answer without understanding access barriers.
The clue 'think about what stands between Priya and it' all but names the answer (distance) when read with the stem.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. A distractor in (a) wrongly suggests speed limits are set by a national law. Question (b) is too easy, and its clue nearly gives the answer away.

proposal.remember: A health service only helps people who can reach and use it.

a.q: Jack, 16, feels very worried late one night. He wants to talk to someone now, without giving his name. Which resource best suits him?
opts: A helpline, open all night, where callers can stay unnamed
A GP clinic in town, which opens at 9 am on weekdays
A school counsellor, who can be seen in the school day
A community health centre, open on weekday afternoons
a.why: Jack needs help now, late at night, and wants to stay unnamed. A helpline is often open at any hour and lets callers keep their name private. The GP, counsellor and health centre are all useful, but none is open late at night, so none suits him right now.
a.clue: Check the time Jack needs help and what he wants to keep private.

b.q: Lena's grandmother moved from Italy and speaks little English. A free community health centre is a ten-minute walk away and opens on Saturdays. A neighbour told her about it, but she has not gone for her sore knee. Which barrier is most likely?
opts: Language, as she speaks little English
Cost, as health centres charge high fees
Distance, as the centre is too far to walk
Opening hours, as the centre is shut at weekends
b.why: The details rule out cost (it is free), distance (a short walk), opening hours (it opens on Saturdays) and not knowing it exists (a neighbour told her). Language is the barrier left. Distance can seem likely for an older person, but a ten-minute walk is close.
b.clue: Check which barriers the details in the story have already removed.
